subject: pathology
title: Calcitonin, Anaplastic Thyroid Cancer, Bethesda System, Parathyroid Adenoma, and Hyperparathyroidism

steps.tx: Calcitonin from parafollicular C cells lowers calcium pharmacologically yet physiologically whispers, serving medicine chiefly as medullary carcinoma's tumour marker and family screening trigger. That marker hormone is **calcitonin in medullary thyroid carcinoma**. Basal calcitonin roughly tracks tumour burden, pentagastrin or calcium stimulation unmasks small C cell disease, and carcinoembryonic antigen rising faster than calcitonin hints at dedifferentiation.
steps.say: Calcitonin treats little physiologically but diagnoses medullary cancer and its families decisively.

steps.tx: Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma dedifferentiates into pleomorphic giant and spindle malignancy invading airways in elderly patients within weeks, among oncology's most lethal tempos demanding airway first planning. That lethal dedifferentiation is **anaplastic thyroid carcinoma**. Median survival is measured in months, every case is staged as advanced at diagnosis, and BRAF testing matters because targeted combinations can shrink selected tumours quickly.
steps.say: Weeks of neck growth in an elderly patient is anaplastic cancer until biopsy acquits it; secure airways first.

vis.caption: Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma invading neck structures at presentation.

steps.tx: Bethesda system reports thyroid cytology in six categories from nondiagnostic through benign, atypia, follicular neoplasm, suspicious, to malignant, each carrying cancer risk and management. That universal language is the **Bethesda system for thyroid cytopathology**. Category II carries a cancer risk near zero to 3 percent, while category VI approaches certainty, so the number attached to the report directly sets the operating plan.
steps.say: Bethesda categories translate thyroid cytology into shared risk numbers and shared decisions.

steps.tx: Parathyroid adenoma, single gland chief cell neoplasm, causes most primary hyperparathyroidism with hypercalcaemia, stones, bones, groans, and psychic moans, sestamibi localising before focused surgery. That single gland culprit is **parathyroid adenoma in primary hyperparathyroidism**. A solitary adenoma explains about 85 percent of cases, four gland hyperplasia most of the rest, and parathyroid carcinoma under 1 percent despite its dramatically high calcium.
steps.say: One adenoma causes most primary hyperparathyroidism; localise it and focused parathyroidectomy cures.

steps.tx: Primary hyperparathyroidism hypercalcaemia with nonsuppressed PTH separates from familial hypocalciuric hypercalcaemia by urine calcium, malignancy PTHrP suppressing PTH instead. That biochemical fork is **hypercalcaemia, PTH dependent versus independent**. A calcium to creatinine clearance ratio below 0.01 favours familial hypocalciuric hypercalcaemia, sparing that family an operation that cannot cure a calcium sensing receptor set point.
steps.say: High calcium asks PTH first: raised means parathyroid or family, suppressed means malignancy and vitamins.

steps.tx: Brown tumours osteoclastically cavitate bones in severe hyperparathyroidism, osteitis fibrosa cystica with subperiosteal resorption, salt and pepper skull, and rugger jersey spine historically. Those resorptive lesions are **brown tumours of hyperparathyroidism**. Subperiosteal resorption shows earliest along the radial side of the middle phalanges, and the brown colour comes from haemorrhage and haemosiderin, not from neoplastic pigment.
steps.say: Brown tumours are osteoclast excavations, not neoplasms; cure the parathyroid and they remineralise.

steps.tx: Intraoperative PTH halving confirms adenoma cure in focused parathyroidectomy, four gland exploration reserving hyperplasia, MEN, and nonlocalised cases. That biochemical assurance is **intraoperative PTH monitoring in parathyroid surgery**. The commonly used criterion asks for a fall of more than 50 percent from the highest pre-excision value at ten minutes after gland removal.
steps.say: PTH halving in theatre signs the cure certificate in focused parathyroid surgery.

steps.tx: Hungry bone syndrome devours calcium into remineralising skeleton after parathyroidectomy for severe disease, tetany risk managed by calcium and calcitriol vigilance. That postoperative sink is **hungry bone syndrome after parathyroidectomy**. Very high preoperative alkaline phosphatase and large adenoma weight predict the plunge, so calcium is checked every six hours or so on the first postoperative day.
steps.say: After curing severe hyperparathyroidism, bones drink calcium hungrily; replace before tetany speaks.
